chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who died and left a wife, and with her, from him, was a child. So she cast him upon a servant of her to breast-feed him. Then she came over seeking the (wages for) breast-feeding the boy, from the successor. So he (peace be upon him) said: ‘For her is a recompense (wages) similar to it, and it is not for the successor that he should throw him out from her lap until he becomes aware (attains puberty), and he should hand over his wealth’.
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a nursing mother and the custody rules for her infant after the father's death according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the financial rights of a widow breastfeeding her infant, establishing that she receives wages comparable to other nurses while retaining custody until the child reaches puberty. It highlights the guardian's (wasi) limited authority to intervene, ensuring the child's wealth is preserved and transferred only upon maturity, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on protecting the orphan's assets during the nursing period.
